text:
mike: quick sanity check — i merged the tf module split into feature/services-refactor and the staging plan shows duplicate provider blocks and a new lockfile churn. worried about state move fallout. can someone eyeball?

anya: looking now. did you hoist the provider out of the module into root? that usually changes addresses if not handled with a shim.

mike: yeah i hoisted the aws provider to root/infra/providers.tf and left the modules referencing source = ../modules/service - but terraform plan shows both module.local.provider and root provider entries. i suspect we need state replace-provider or a provider_alias fix. plan snippet:
```
# plan excerpt
- module.service.aws_s3_bucket.main will be replaced
+ provider[registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws] (new version)
```

deploy-bot: CI started: terraform plan (staging) — job #4021. plan will post when finished.

sarah: if addresses changed you have two choices: 1) run `terraform state replace-provider` to map old addresses to new provider addresses, or 2) do a small migration PR that keeps the provider block in-module but marked deprecated, then do a follow-up to hoist. doing replace-provider is faster but be careful with remote state locks.

jordan: also check .terraform.lock.hcl — module refactors often bump provider checksums if registry mirror or provider version constraint was loosened. Did you change any provider version constraints?

mike: nope constraints same (`>= 3.0, < 4.0`). the lockfile changed though. diff shows hash changes for hashicorp/aws and hashicorp/random. seems like the CI ran `terraform init -upgrade` accidentally.

anya: ok that explains lock churn. revert the lockfile change in the refactor PR and run plan again without -upgrade. we want to keep deterministic checksums for the staging workspace until we intentionally bump providers.

mike: noted. for the provider address migration, example command i plan to run: `terraform state replace-provider 'module.service.aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws'` anyone see an issue?

sarah: the syntax is `terraform state replace-provider old-provider new-provider` where providers are like `registry.terraform.io/-/aws` vs `registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws` depending on version. run `terraform providers` first to confirm exact addresses. also ensure you have a state backup. :warning:

jordan: one more gotcha: our k8s secret wiring for service credentials used the module output `secret_path = module.service.secret_path`. after the split the output name is the same but path root changed in kustomize. verify the Helm/kustomize overlay still points to the same secret name. i hit an outage last time when secret path changed.

mike: good call. i checked the kustomize overlays — service overlay references `secretRef: service-credentials` which is produced by the module output. looks OK but i'll run a quick `kubectl -n staging get secret service-credentials -o yaml` after the plan.

anya: if you want, i can review the replace-provider command before you apply. also add a short note in the PR description about lockfile revert and why. that helps oncall if there is follow-up. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — i'll revert the lockfile change, rerun plan, paste the exact `terraform state replace-provider` args here for a quick check, then request lgtm.

deploy-bot: plan finished: no-destroy diff detected. detailed plan: https://ci.redwood/terraform/4021/plan.html

jordan: 👍 looks good from infra side. run the replace-provider in a maintenance window if you want to be extra safe.

mike: will do, thanks everyone. closing this thread after the PR update.
